note: A peer-supplied Parent Response carries the Challenge TLV that seeds the stored challenge bytes and length.
The parsed Challenge TLV length is copied into the child-id request state and later reused when generating a response.
The attacker-controlled challenge bytes are stored in the fixed-size child-id request buffer.
When the device later builds a Child Update Response, it emits a Response TLV using the stored challenge state.
The stored challenge length is passed directly into AppendResponse, so any oversized length becomes the TLV length for serialization.
AppendResponse writes that length into the Response TLV header without bounding it to the 8-byte payload buffer.
The oversized TLV is appended to the outgoing message, which forwards the same length into the buffer write path.
Serialization copies bytes from the ResponseTlv object past its fixed mResponse array, causing the stack-buffer-overflow read sink.
ResponseTlv contains only an 8-byte response buffer, so any length above 8 makes the serializer read beyond the object boundary.
